newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivorian president says reshuffle not imminent.
newsitem.headline: Ivorian president says reshuffle not imminent.

text.p: Ivory Coast's president, Henri Konan Bedie, said on Wednesday that he still planned to open his government to members of the opposition but played down talk of an imminent reshuffle.
Bedie, in remarks to state television ahead of a cabinet meeting in Ivory Coast's inland political capital Yamoussoukro, said contacts with likely interested parties were continuing.
"I have already announced it (a plan for such a government) but it is not for right now in the sense that we are continuing discussions with those likely to take part," he said.

Newspapers and political commentators speculated that Wednesday's meeting in Yamoussoukro, birthplace of late independence president Felix Houphouet-Boigny, could see a government reshuffle following December 29 by-elections that wrapped up the country's second multi-party national elections.

Laurent Gbagbo, leader of the mainstream opposition Ivorian Popular Front (FPI), won election to parliament just outside his centre west Gagnoa stronghold -- over one year after the rest of the country voted in legislative elections.
Gagnoa region polling was postponed from November 1995 after political and ethnic violence surrounding Bedie's October 1995 presidential election victory killed 25 people in the region.

The other main opposition party is the Rally of the Republicans (RDR) composed of defectors from Bedie's ruling Democratic Party (PDCI). Both opposition groups have 13 seats each in the 175-seat national assembly.

The television and the government newspaper Fraternite Matin portrayed the Yamoussoukro meeting as aimed at reinforcing the role of the inland capital, which plays a minor role in the life of the nation compared to Abidjan, the commercial capital.
